title: Rasuwa–Bhotekoshi Ice-Rock Avalanche & Debris Flood
hazard: Ice-rock avalanche → temporary blockage → debris flood
region: Lhende Khola → Bhotekoshi → Trishuli, Rasuwa District
detectedChange: Ice-rock detachment on the north face of Langtang Lirung; channel blockage in the Lhende Khola
summary: A slab of rock and glacier ice detached from the north face of Langtang Lirung (7,227 m) shortly after 08:37 NPT on 26 August 2026, fell about 1,200 m into the Lhende Khola on the Nepal–China border, briefly blocked the channel and released a sediment-laden debris flood down the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli. ICIMOD stresses this was an ice-rock avalanche cascade, not a classic glacial-lake outburst: no pre-existing lake has been shown to be the source, and DHM reported no heavy rainfall in Rasuwa immediately before the flood. The July 2025 Rasuwagadhi flood is precursor context only.

mparams.label: Glacier Geometry
mparams.source: ICIMOD field/satellite reconstruction of the 26 Aug 2026 detachment. Elevation and fall height as stated by ICIMOD — verified. Ice thickness: not measured.

mparams.label: Ice / Snow
metrics: M5.2, reclassified by USGS as landslide
mparams.source: USGS reclassified the initially reported M4.4 earthquake as an M5.2 landslide source — verified. Glacier area is an approximate catchment estimate, not a measured inventory value.

mparams.label: Crack & Instability
mparams.source: ICIMOD and CARE/ICIMOD reporting: a barrier lake formed by the initial debris broke on 28 August, briefly halting rescue in Nepal and China — verified.

mparams.label: Glacial Lakes
mparams.source: NDRRMA warned of continuing flood risk from an estimated 0.11 km² lake formed upstream by the blockage of the Lhende Khola (via WFP situation report) — verified. Any lake here is a temporary landslide-dammed lake, not a glacial lake.

mparams.label: Hydrology
metrics: 57.4 million m³ (≈19.96 M m³ above base flow)
mparams.source: DHM gauge record and NDRRMA volume estimate, compiled in the ICIMOD/partner story map — verified. Galchhi is ≈88 km downstream of the source.

mparams.label: Weather / Climate
metrics: No substantial rain before the event
mparams.source: Nepal DHM reported no substantial rainfall in Rasuwa immediately before the flood — verified. This is the key reason investigators looked upstream. Temperature anomaly is an approximate regional figure, not a station measurement.

mparams.label: Terrain
mparams.source: ICIMOD explanation of why Rasuwagadhi and Timure were worst hit: the Lhende drops from over 5,000 m to about 1,800 m at the border, and the first flat ground is where the dry port, truck park and hydropower works were built — verified narrative; slope value approximate.

mparams.label: Infrastructure
metrics: Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, Upper Trishuli 3A/3B, Trishuli, Devighat
mparams.source: WFP situation report (≈40 km roads, >80 bridges, ≥14 hydropower/energy facilities) and Nepal Electricity Authority (13 projects, ≈431 MW off-grid, ≈470 MW under construction damaged) — verified as reported.

mparams.label: Exposure
mparams.source: Figures as reported by NDRRMA / Nepal Police and compiled on the Wikipedia "2026 Nepal floods" index, retrieved 20 Sep 2026. Search, rescue and identification are ongoing — these numbers change and are NOT final.

mparams.label: Response Resources
mparams.source: NDRRMA Rasuwa–Bhotekoshi Search, Rescue and Relief Situation Report #01, 1 Sep 2026 — verified as reported on that date.

mlNotes.lake_area_km2: V — 0.11 km² barrier lake (NDRRMA via WFP)
mlNotes.lake_growth_pct_yr: S — proxy only; a blockage is instantaneous, there is no real growth series

why: Ice-rock slab detached from the Langtang Lirung north face and fell ≈1,200 m into the Lhende Khola (ICIMOD)
Channel blockage formed and released — barrier lake of ≈0.11 km² later breached on 28 Aug (NDRRMA)
Trishuli rose ≈9 m in 30 minutes at Galchhi, 88 km downstream — almost no warning time
Dense border infrastructure (dry port, truck park, hydropower) sits on the first flat riverbed at Rasuwagadhi
Rainfall was ruled out by DHM, so no rainfall-based warning would have been triggered
